transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you. Could you tell me a little bit about what brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. Um... I came in today because I just can’t seem to shake this really heavy, hopeless feeling. It's... well, it feels like everything I managed to build back up after my divorce has just collapsed, and I’m just sitting under the weight of it. I just don't know how to get out from under it right now.
Have you experienced these feelings of hopelessness and heaviness in the past, perhaps in a distinct period before this current situation?

Um... I don't think so. I mean, I've had hard days or felt sad before, but... not this kind of heavy. I haven't really noticed feeling this completely stuck and hopeless in the past. It just sort of... feels like it's all just happening right now.
Since this feeling started, have you noticed any significant changes in your sleep patterns?

Yeah, it's been pretty bad. Um... lately, I either just lie awake staring at the ceiling, replaying my bills or... or mistakes I've made at work. Or if I do manage to drop off, I end up waking up way before dawn, and I just feel like I never actually slept at all. It's really exhausting.
Have you found that you are no longer interested in or able to enjoy the activities or hobbies that you usually find pleasurable?

I'm not really sure. Um... I haven't really noticed losing interest in things, exactly. I mean, I haven't been doing much outside of work lately, but... I don't think it's that I can't enjoy my hobbies anymore. I just haven't really tried doing them.

When you think about how you've been feeling, do you feel like these symptoms are a direct reaction to the stress of your divorce and these recent work problems, or does it feel like something else is going on that would be there even if those things were resolved?

I honestly don't know. Um... it's hard to separate it all out. The divorce and the issues at work are definitely a huge part of what's going on right now, but... I'm not really sure if I'd still feel this heavy if all of that just got fixed. It just feels like one big mess right now, so I couldn't really say for sure.
Have you noticed any changes in your physical energy or the speed at which you move or speak, such as feeling physically slowed down or, conversely, feeling restless and unable to sit still?

Not really, no. I mean... I feel tired, obviously, because of the sleep issues. But I don't think I'm moving or talking any slower than normal. And I'm not pacing around or feeling restless, either. I'm just... physically drained, I guess, but my actual speed seems about the same.
Have you noticed any change in your appetite or your weight since these feelings began?

Um... no, not really. My appetite seems pretty normal. I haven't been weighing myself or anything, but my clothes still fit exactly the same, so I don't think my weight has changed. I'm just eating about what I usually do.
Do you find yourself dwelling on feelings of worthlessness or experiencing excessive guilt about the things going on in your life?

Yes, I do. Um... I just keep telling myself that I'm a terrible engineer and a failed wife. I feel like a burden to everyone right now. I find myself constantly replaying every missed calculation from work or... or every tense email I've sent, and it just feels like proof that I ruin things. So, yeah, I dwell on that a lot.
Have you noticed any difficulty with your concentration, such as trouble focusing on tasks at work or even following a television show or book?

Yes, definitely. It's actually been a huge problem at work. I'll look at a basic drainage calculation or a spreadsheet I've used for years, and... my mind just completely blanks. I just sit there rereading the same numbers over and over, and I can't even trust myself to make a simple decision about them. It's like I just can't focus on it at all.
Beyond the difficulty you're having with your focus at work, has this heavy feeling caused you to miss work, avoid seeing friends or family, or stop taking care of your usual daily responsibilities?

Yeah, it's... it's affected pretty much everything. At work, it wasn't just the focus. I was making some really questionable calls on my projects, and I kept falling apart during meetings. My supervisor actually had to step in and take me off all active project decisions. 

And at home, I just... I completely stopped keeping up with my basic routines. I wasn't doing much of anything. It actually got bad enough that I ended up being sent to the emergency department recently, just because... well, I didn't feel safe alone with my own thoughts anymore. So, yes, it's made it impossible to keep up with my life.

Looking back at the past few weeks, do you feel that the intensity of your emotional pain and the complete inability to function in your daily life is a normal reaction to your recent stressors, or does it feel disproportionately severe and overwhelming compared to what you would expect?

I... I think it's disproportionately severe. I mean, yes, I've had some stress at work, but this... this is completely overwhelming. I've been stressed before, and I never ended up in the emergency room because I couldn't trust myself to be alone. It just feels like everything is completely broken, way beyond what a normal reaction to stress should be.
